Per: Justice Anuradha Shukla Appellant-State has preferred this leave to appeal under Section 378(iii) of the Cr.P.C. against the impugned judgment dated 16.04.2013 passed by learned First Additional Sessions Judge, Harda, District Harda (M.P.) in ST No.31/2011 whereby the respondent No.1 and 2 were acquitted from Sections 342, 363, 376(chha) and 506 II of IPC, respondents No. 3 and 4 from Sections 363 of IPC and respondent No.5 from 342/34 and 363/34 of IPC.

2. Brief facts of the case are that minor prosecutrix aged 16 years was alone near culvert when respondent No.2. Deepak told her that she is being summoned by her brother and when she went along with Deepak to the field of Bhawani Rajput, respondent No.1 Mukesh was there alongwith juvenile 2 CRA-2981-2013 delinquent.
Mukesh proposed to marry her and upon resentment of prosecutrix, forcibly took her behind the tree and raped her.
She was also raped by Deepak and the juvenile delinquent.
Mukesh then took her in a vehicle and respondents No.3 Ashok @ Pappu and 4 Ramchandra were also riding that vehicle.
Prosecutrix went unconscious and when she gained consciousness she found herself in confinement in a room.
Mukesh then took her to Bhopal in a car and there prosecutrix went to her relatives house.
She intimated the relative about the incident and thereafter the matter was reported to the police on 09.10.2010.
FIR was registered against all the respondents and also against the juvenile delinquent at crime No.298/2010.

After investigation,
charge-sheet was filed and upon conclusion of trial, the impugned judgment acquitting all the respondents of all charges was passed.
3. The grounds raised in this appeal are that the impugned judgment is illegal and perverse, hence deserves interference.

It has been argued that the impugned judgment is incorrect, improper and The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Mukesh on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120432538/

sentences.text: The trial Court could not properly appreciate the evidence and given the perverse finding and acquitted the respondents.
It placed undue weightage on minor omissions and contradictions while the guilt of respondents was proved beyond doubt.
4. We have heard and considered the arguments submitted on behalf of the appellant-State and have also gone through the impugned judgment as well as the entire record of the trial court.

5. From the perusal of record, it is evident that the FIR of this crime of gang rape was lodged with a delay of three days and the MLC report of 3 CRA-2981-2013 prosecutrix was not proved through the medical officer who had examined her.
Even otherwise that MLC report suggest that no marks of injuries were found on the body of prosecutrix and no definite opinion was given about the commission of crime.
The learned counsel for the appellant is placing heavy reliance on the FSL report (Ex.P/30), but that is not a conclusive evidence.
If the oral testimony of prosecution witness is analyzed, it is established that prosecutrix was not consistent in her statements.
The FIR (Ex.P/29) claims that she was first raped by Mukesh and then by other respondents, but in her Court testimony, she has insisted that Mukesh was not present at the scene of crime.
FIR does not claim that she was raped by Ramchandra and Pappu, but her Court testimony places guilt on these two respondents also.
PW/2 is the mother of prosecutrix and according to her rape was committed with her daughter by respondent Deepak, Ramchandra and Pappu and by none other.
The statements of father of prosecutrix (PW/3) suggest that he had no knowledge of the incident of rape.
According to him, his daughter went missing for which a missing person report was lodged.
His statements further damage the prosecution case.
The brother of prosecutrix examined as PW/4 and he has given a completely hostile testimony by denying any crime committed with his real sister.

Taking the non-supporting and inconsistent testimony of prosecution witnesses into consideration,
the trial Court arrived at the finding of acquittal.

6. In the judgments of State of Karnataka Vs. Gopal Krishna (2005) 9 SCC 291 , Girija Prasad Vs.
State of M.P. (2007) 7 SCC 625 and Phool Singh vs. State of Himachal Pradesh AIR 2014 SC 1256 , it has been observed that if 4 CRA-2981-2013 unreasonable or perverse findings are given by the Court below, the appellate Court is required to interfere as it has ample power to appreciate, review and reconsider the evidence as a whole and that the Court must act responsibly and sensitively in such matters.
